messages.content:
A store buys widgets at $4.20 each and sells them at a 35% markup on the purchase price. On Tuesday it sold 140 widgets. However, 15% of Tuesday's sales were returned for a full refund (the store keeps the returned widgets and has no restocking cost).

What was the store's net sales revenue from the widgets that were NOT returned, in dollars? Round to the nearest cent.


When you are finished, output your final answer on its own line, as the last line of your response, in the exact format:
ANSWER: <your answer>

text:
First, calculate the selling price of each widget. The store marks up the purchase price by 35%:
$$ \text{Selling Price} = \$4.20 \times (1 + 0.35) $$
$$ \text{Selling Price} = \$4.20 \times 1.35 $$
$$ \text{Selling Price} = \$5.67 $$

Next, determine how many widgets were kept after the returns. Since 15% of sales were returned, 85% (or $1 - 0.15$) were not returned:
$$ \text{Widgets Sold and Kept} = 140 \times 0.85 $$
$$ \text{Widgets Sold and Kept} = 119 $$

Finally, calculate the net sales revenue from these widgets by multiplying the number kept by the selling price per widget:
$$ \text{Net Sales Revenue} = 119 \times \$5.67 $$
$$ \text{Net Sales Revenue} = \$674.73 $$

ANSWER: 674.73
